perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s available perspective, I know/experienced:

- I am a salesperson at a marketing firm and work with Katherine Lasiloo, the marketing manager. Our relationship is professional but can be strained by differing views on sales and marketing strategy.
- I prepared data and charts from our last five campaigns to support traditional sales techniques. In a meeting room, I told Katherine that I appreciated her innovative digital strategies but believed our core sales could benefit more from traditional methods, and that proven methods felt sidelined without proper consideration. I clarified I was not suggesting we abandon digital marketing.
- I heard Katherine say she saw my point, that the market is evolving, that digital outreach and increasing online engagement can’t be ignored, and that we should analyze the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories. I told her the results were impressive and asked how those strategies are developed. She explained it is about targeting the right audience with the right message and offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making process. I admitted I had doubts about moving away from traditional methods but wanted to understand the digital approach more. She said adapting and evolving with market trends is important and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- I proposed a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital marketing. Katherine agreed, saying combining our strengths could lead to better results, and we planned to schedule/brainstorm next steps.
- After the joint meeting, I was excited, worked overtime, and drafted a board presentation integrating both our ideas. I told Katherine I was excited about it and wanted to nail the presentation. She reviewed it, called it comprehensive and well thought out, and praised my hard work. I said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart from competitors. She said she was confident and suggested fine-tuning it together.
- After the presentation and implementation, I thanked Katherine and said I had learned and grown through our collaboration. She said it was a pleasure seeing the project come to fruition and that my openness made it a successful partnership. I proposed regular strategy sessions; she agreed, saying they would keep us on top of our game and market trends.

I do not have access to Katherine’s private thoughts or motivations beyond what she said or did, nor to narrator-only summaries.
